description:
The first arm of the ordered blank-field chain, :118-122, driven through its LOW-VALUES half. EVALUATE TRUE at :117 is ordered and the first matching WHEN wins; WHEN USERIDI OF COSGN0AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES is a two-term disjunction, and here it is the second term that answers - the user id arrives as eight X'00' bytes, which is the image a symbolic-map field carries when the terminal put no data into it. :119 moves 'Y' into WS-ERR-FLG, :120 moves 'Please enter User ID ...' into WS-MESSAGE, :121 moves -1 into USERIDL and :122 performs SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN. The password carries a real eight-byte value, so :123 is false and cannot have produced this message; that is what isolates the LOW-VALUES term here from the ordering question case08 answers by blanking both fields at once. :138 then finds ERR-FLG-ON true, so READ-USER-SEC-FILE is never performed and USRSEC is never opened.

The item is declared explicitly at eight X'00' bytes rather than omitted from mapFields. Omitting it would arrive at the same image, because an absent field is read as LOW-VALUES at its declared width, but only the explicit form states on the page which of the two terms this case exists to drive - case08 is the case that omits. X'00' is emphatically not X'20', and that distinction is what makes the two terms independently falsifiable: a translation testing String.isBlank() would report eight X'00' as non-blank, miss this arm, fall through to WHEN OTHER at :128-129 and use the nulls as a key, answering 'User not found. Try again ...' instead of 'Please enter User ID ...'; one testing trim().isEmpty() would pass here and still be wrong, because it would also report a field mixing spaces and nulls as blank where the COBOL treats it as data. The SPACES half of this same arm is pinned separately, by the blank-user-id ValueSource in SignOnServiceTest which drives eight spaces, and case08 pins that the earlier arm speaks when both halves match together.

CDEMO-USER-ID is X'00' eight times over rather than eight spaces, and that is not an oversight. :132-134 sits after END-EVALUATE and outside every arm of it, so MOVE FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI) TO WS-USER-ID, CDEMO-USER-ID runs unconditionally - on this rejected path exactly as on the signing-on path - and FUNCTION UPPER-CASE alters only lower-case alphabetics, passing every other byte through untouched. X'00' is not a lower-case letter, so the normalisation is an identity move here and the communication area carries eight null bytes in a PIC X(08) span. That is precisely what the COBOL leaves there: folding the normalisation into the success path, or quietly normalising the nulls to spaces, would each show up here as a diff. It is also the one substantive expectation that separates this case from its SPACES twin, where the very same unconditional move yields eight spaces instead.

USERIDO and PASSWDO are the map's own storage rather than payload members. app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:85 declares 01 COSGN0AO REDEFINES COSGN0AI, and within each field the input view spends xxxL plus xxxF plus a four-byte FILLER - seven bytes - exactly where the output view spends a three-byte FILLER plus xxxC, xxxP, xxxH and xxxV, so USERIDI at :72 and USERIDO at :140 occupy the same eight bytes at the same width. No paragraph of COSGN00C moves anything into either output item; the program reads USERIDI at :118 and :132 and PASSWDI at :123 and :135 and repositions the cursor through the length items. EIBCALEN is 160 here, so MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COSGN0AO at :81 did not run, and what those two hold at SEND time is simply what RECEIVE MAP left: the received images, eight X'00' for the id and PASSWORD for the password. SignOnResponse carries neither item, so the JSON payload never echoes a credential.

USRSEC is seeded from app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose ten in-stream rows are 57 characters where app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy declares 80: SEC-USR-ID X(08) at 0, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 8, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 28, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 48, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 56 - which is 57 - then SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 57, which is 80. The 23-byte shortfall is supplied once at seed time by the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation and never hand-padded, and the 80-character expectedFinalState images prove that span was emitted as 23 spaces - a record missing it would be short by exactly 23. The same job corroborates the target width twice, with DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) on SYSUT2 and RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) on the cluster. The dataset is addressed by its binding key USRSEC - the CICS file name at :39 - and never by a dataset name. expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion: COSGN00C contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE on any path, and the read at :211-219 does not even specify UPDATE, so it takes no lock and holds no record. expectedReturnCode is 0 because grep -c RETURN-CODE over the program is 0.

Determinism and the two substitutions. POPULATE-HEADER-INFO opens with MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CURDATE-DATA at :179, so the clock is pinned rather than read: 2022-07-19T23:12:33, traceable to this program's own version footer at :259 and expressed as a fixed local date-time so no timezone can shift it. Through app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY is MM '/' DD '/' YY with YY taken from WS-CURDATE-YEAR(3:2), giving CURDATEO exactly 07/19/22 at its PIC X(8); WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS is HH ':' MM ':' SS, eight bytes, moved into CURTIMEO which app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:122 declares PIC X(9) - hence 23:12:33 followed by exactly one trailing space. Note that width: the sibling COUSR02 map declares its CURTIMEO PIC X(8) and the two must not be conflated. APPLID and SYSID come from EXEC CICS ASSIGN at :198-204, which has no Java equivalent and which neither application.yml nor application-test.yml binds, so CICSAWS1 and AWS1 space-padded to PIC X(8) are pinned constants standing in for those two calls; all twenty cases use the same pair, and the substitution is stated rather than hidden.

Provenance. Every expected value above is statically derived - by structured reading of app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the record layout, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the communication area, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy and app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy and app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the literals and the header, app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY with app/bms/COSGN00.bms for the screen field shapes, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD for transaction CC00, and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 for the ten seed rows. It was never captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand.

The unit is SignOnService, driven as a plain object with a fixture-backed SecUserRepository, and the eleven-field screen is projected by SignOnController, also a plain object - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path. All conversation state travels in the payload, so no server-side session exists to hold any of it. The password stays plaintext because app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:223 compares it in plaintext; that is an inherited property of the legacy design and an explicit non-goal of this migration, not something to correct here. Neither the backward-GO TO restructuring gate nor the abend gate applies: grep -c "GO TO" and grep -c CEE3ABD over app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl are both 0, and neither is faked. No file operation occurs on this path either, so the file-status gate is not exercised here rather than being satisfied by a fabricated read. Two further absences are recorded rather than papered over: :59 reads *COPY DFHATTR., which is a comment because the asterisk sits in column 7, so no DFHATTR attribute constant applies to this screen at all; and COSGN00C copies CSSETATY nowhere, so there is no runtime DFHRED plus '*' highlight to assert and attributes is empty for that reason and not by omission. The error emphasis on this path is the -1 cursor request at :121 together with ERRMSG's static ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) and COLOR=RED at app/bms/COSGN00.bms:197-200, which the map carries whether or not a message is present.
